results.fact: Compass direction of the 6,800 ft gully crossing
results.evidence: The route description says to follow the south ridge to about 6,800 ft, then head left across gullies to the gentler southwest slope. USGS 1 m elevation samples across the ridge (lat 48.5115-48.5145) put the south ridge crest at about lng -120.708 running north-south, with gentler ground falling to the WEST (e.g. 7,130 -> 6,787 -> 6,543 -> 5,932 ft westward at lat 48.513) and steeper ground to the east; north along the ridge is uphill toward the summit, not across gullies. So 'left' while climbing a south ridge is west, onto the southwest slope.

results.evidence: Still only one source states the split (about 5,300 ft to Honeymoon Meadows plus about 4,000 ft on the summit day, ~9,300 ft); another trip report gives about 5,000 ft for the ~17 mile walk in, and the hike page for the West Fork trail alone gives 2,400 ft, so the day-1 figure and the car-to-car total do not converge. gain_ft 5,706 is a net-rise figure no source states. Would settle: a GPS-measured car-to-car total for the Dosewallips road end -> Honeymoon Meadows -> White Mountain trip.
No outside source states a car-to-car descent figure for this route, and loss_ft may not be derived from gain or the itinerary. Would settle: a sourced car-to-car loss figure.

results.fact: Honeymoon Meadows to Anderson Pass leg
results.correct_value: about 950 ft of gain from Honeymoon Meadows (distance more than 1.2 mi; stated value removed)
results.evidence: USGS point elevations at the row's own pins read 3,536 ft at Honeymoon Meadows and 4,477 ft at Anderson Pass (~940 ft); published figures of 3,527 ft for Honeymoon Meadows and 4,464 ft for Anderson Pass give the same ~940 ft, so '700 ft' is wrong (700 ft is the figure for the shorter hop to Camp Siberia). On distance, a mile log puts Honeymoon Meadows at 14.15 mi and the pass at 16.0 mi (1.85 mi) and a separate family trip report says Camp Siberia alone is 1.3 mi past Honeymoon Meadows, so '~1.2 mi' understates it; the exact figure is not agreed by two sources, so the number is removed rather than replaced.

results.evidence: The trail and route pages (hike description, mile-by-mile trail guide, lookout history page, lookout list page) all say only that a steep, exposed snowfield near the top/above the switchbacks lingers into July-August and that the slope 'above' must be traversed; none names its aspect. One page notes the trail crosses the treeless southeast slope, which fits the approach wording but does not say where the snow lies. Would settle: a trip report or photo naming which face the lingering snow traverse crosses.

Sources genuinely disagree: the hike page gives 11.0 mi one-way from Long Swamp (matching the row's 22 mi RT), while a lookout-history page says 'Seven miles by Trail 342 ... starting at Long Swamp', another lookout page calls it the 7-mile Windy Peak Trail, and a 2004 trip report says the trail from Long Swamp is 12 miles round trip. The straight line from the trailhead pin to the summit is only ~5.1 mi, which favours the shorter figure, but changing it would rewrite dist_km, itinerary, hazards, timing and every waypoint distMi against the one detailed source. Would settle: a GPS track of Trail 342 from Long Swamp to the summit.

Two genuine options: one route page says parties coming from the south can make a blocky scramble up the south side of the summit pyramid or stay on the trail across a west-facing basin to the easy west side, and another says the easy class 2 way is the west slope with the south and north ridges harder. The rope note names the easy west-slope line and the approach variant describes the south-side scramble from the trail's high point south of the summit; both exist.

The trailhead's mapped location (48.8228, -120.0197, matching the row's pin) reads 3,447 ft on the USGS 1 m elevation service; trail-mapping sites give the Chewuch Trail's low point at its Thirtymile end as 1,045 m (~3,430 ft) and ~3,440 ft. The ~3,600 ft figure in four prose fields is ~150-200 ft too high; the waypoint's 3,400 ft is right.
